clue.text: Press employee, sort with dog in tow

indicators.note: something in tow is pulled along behind, so the dog comes after the sort

parts.note: a sort is a piece of metal type in printing
a setter is a breed of gun dog

explanation.surface: A printing-works employee who brings a dog along to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort' reads as a verb but is the printer's noun for a single piece of type.
explanation.definitionFit: A typesetter works at a printing press arranging type for printing.

clue.text: Openness of projectable photo?

definitions.meaning: the quality of being open and frank
a photographic slide shown with a projector

explanation.surface: Asking whether a frank attitude belongs to a slide.
explanation.definitionFit: Transparency means candour, and is also a slide or film image viewed by projection.

clue.text: Horse having drink by entrance to orchard?

parts.note: a pint is a drink of beer

indicators.note: the entrance of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of orchard is used

explanation.surface: A horse enjoying a drink at the orchard gate.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinto is a piebald or skewbald horse, a breed name popular in America.

clue.text: Utter anarchy at first in outskirts of Sydney

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the outer one
the outskirts of a place are its edges, so the outer letters of Sydney
at first points to the opening letter of the word anarchy

explanation.surface: Total chaos breaking out on the edge of an Australian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utter' looks like an adjective (complete) to go with anarchy, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To utter something is to say it out loud.

clue.text: He painted innocents originally gobbled up by giant

indicators.note: being gobbled up by something puts it inside, so this letter goes within the giant

parts.note: a titan is a giant

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of innocents

explanation.surface: A fairy-tale picture of innocents swallowed by a giant.
explanation.definitionFit: Titian was a great Venetian painter of the Renaissance.

clue.text: Corrected English males, old-fashioned

parts.note: males are men
something old-fashioned is dated

explanation.surface: A complaint that English men are behind the times.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend a text is to correct its errors, so emendated means put right.

clue.text: Way wet weather produces stress

parts.note: ST, short for street, is a way
rain is wet weather

explanation.surface: Rainy conditions make life stressful.
explanation.definitionFit: Strain and stress are synonyms for pressure or tension.

clue.text: What criminal offences may not be, but some batteries are?

definitions.text: What criminal offences may not be, but some batteries are?

parts.words: What criminal offences may not be, but some batteries are?
parts.note: an offence that has been tried may not be charged again, while some batteries can be recharged

explanation.surface: A riddle comparing legal charges with batteries.
explanation.walkthrough: The word splits as RE-CHARGEABLE in the legal sense: double jeopardy forbids charging someone again for the same offence.
explanation.definitionFit: Rechargeable batteries can be refilled with electrical power and reused.

clue.text: Irritate a small number in US city

indicators.note: in puts the number inside the city's letters

parts.note: NY is New York
NO is the short form of number

explanation.surface: A small number of people causing irritation in New York.
explanation.definitionFit: To annoy someone is to irritate them; the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Consume refreshments initially in the Criterion, perhaps

indicators.note: in puts these letters inside the word the

parts.note: to consume food is to eat

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of refreshments

explanation.surface: Eating refreshments at the Criterion, perhaps a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: The Criterion is both a famous London restaurant and the theatre at Piccadilly Circus; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Criterion Theatre in London is an example of a playhouse.

clue.text: Vertically challenged worker's system of writing?

parts.note: a jokey euphemism for short
a hand is a manual worker

explanation.surface: A short employee's own method of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Shorthand is a rapid writing method using abbreviations and symbols, as Pitman or Gregg.

clue.text: One putting up with moving to art role

indicators.note: moving the letters around rearranges them into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone tolerant enough to switch to a role in art.
explanation.definitionFit: A tolerator is someone who tolerates, that is, puts up with things.

clue.text: A second husband's remains

explanation.surface: A widow keeping her second husband's ashes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remains' looks like a verb but is the noun for what is left after burning.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash is the residue left after something has burned, including cremated human remains.

clue.text: Horrify a namesake of Revere when speaking

indicators.note: when speaking says the answer sounds like these words said out loud

parts.note: Paul Revere, the American patriot of the midnight ride, so a namesake is a Paul

explanation.surface: Someone sharing Paul Revere's name horrifying listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul Revere was the American silversmith famed for his ride warning of the British advance in 1775.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal is to shock or horrify; it is the British spelling.

clue.text: Cutting tool one of two PMs reportedly observed

indicators.note: reportedly says the name sounds like the piece entered

parts.note: William Pitt the Elder and his son William Pitt the Younger were both British Prime Ministers
observed means saw

explanation.surface: A prime minister witnessed with a cutting tool.
explanation.walkthrough: Two British PMs were called Pitt, father and son, in the 18th century.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitsaw is a large two-man saw once used over a pit for cutting timber.

clue.text: Person singing some forgotten oratorio

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A singer performing in a neglected oratorio.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenor is a male singer with a high voice, often a soloist in oratorios.

clue.text: Austere city state once, not all in South Africa

indicators.note: in puts the part inside the country's letters

parts.note: a part is not all of something

explanation.surface: A former city state, only partly found in South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparta was the ancient Greek city state famous for its harsh, spartan way of life.

clue.text: Film about female amphibian

indicators.note: about means going round, so the film's letters surround the female

parts.note: ET is the Spielberg film about an alien
F is the abbreviation for female; the answer also running backwards across about female is a coincidence

explanation.surface: A film about a female amphibian.
explanation.definitionFit: An eft is a newt, a small amphibian, especially a young one.

clue.text: Don't accept note with sweet I consumed

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
pud, short for pudding, is a British word for a sweet course
consumed means ate

explanation.surface: Refusing a note sent with a dessert one had eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: To repudiate is to reject or refuse to accept something.

clue.text: In maturity some soldiers see eye to eye

indicators.note: In puts the soldiers inside the word for maturity

parts.note: age is maturity
RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army

explanation.surface: Older soldiers finding they think alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people who see eye to eye share the same view, so they concur.

clue.text: Small talk primarily concerning manufacturer of headgear

indicators.note: primarily points to the first letter of concerning

parts.note: a hatter makes hats

explanation.surface: Gossip mainly about a hat maker.
explanation.definitionFit: Chatter is light, idle conversation, the same as small talk.

clue.text: Get rid of stunted vegetation

definitions.meaning: to ... a plan is to cancel or get rid of it
land covered with low, stunted bushes

explanation.surface: Clearing away undergrowth.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrub means cancel informally, and also low shrubby growth on poor land.

clue.text: Young relative — one that shines, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the answer sounds like this word

parts.note: the sun is what shines in the sky

explanation.surface: A shining youngster in the family.
explanation.definitionFit: A son is a male child, a younger member of the family.

clue.text: Large French resort visited by European relative

parts.note: large means great

indicators.note: being visited by someone means having them inside, so the European goes within the resort

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera

explanation.surface: A big French seaside town receiving a European visitor.
explanation.definitionFit: A great-niece is the granddaughter of one's brother or sister, a family member.
